subject: pathology
title: Rheumatic, valvular heart disease and endocarditis

steps.tx: **Rheumatic fever** follows group A streptococcal pharyngitis in susceptible hosts after a gap of weeks. Cross reactive immunity injures the heart, joints, skin and brain during the illness. Carditis with **Aschoff bodies** is the pathological signature, and repeated attacks scar valves into chronic rheumatic heart disease. Jones criteria organise diagnosis, while echocardiography reveals subclinical carditis that older criteria missed.
steps.say: Rheumatic fever follows streptococcal throat infection by several weeks. Cross reactive immunity injures the heart and other tissues. Aschoff bodies are marking carditis within the myocardium on biopsy. Repeated attacks scar the valves into chronic disease.

steps.tx: The **Aschoff body** is a perivascular granulomatous focus that contains T cells, plasma cells and distinctive macrophages. Those macrophages are Anitschkov cells whose chromatin resembles a **caterpillar**, and occasional multinucleate giant cells appear. Acute valvulitis warps leaflets and places small vegetations along closure lines without destruction. Chronic healing fuses commissures and narrows the mitral orifice into a fish mouth shape over years.
steps.say: The Aschoff body holds macrophages whose chromatin resembles a caterpillar. Acute valvulitis is placing small vegetations along the closure lines. The valve leaflets warp but they are not destroyed. Chronic healing fuses commissures and narrows the mitral opening.

steps.tx: This section shows myocardium around a circumscribed **Aschoff body**, which is the signature lesion of rheumatic carditis. Inside the focus, an **Anitschkov caterpillar cell** shows wavy central chromatin and a **multinucleate giant cell** sits nearby. Recognising these cells lets the student link a microscopy stem to acute rheumatic fever. The lesion sits between muscle fibres rather than destroying a valve leaflet directly.
steps.say: This section shows an Aschoff body sitting within the myocardium. The caterpillar cell is showing distinctive wavy central chromatin inside. A multinucleate giant cell is lying near the inflammatory focus. These features identify rheumatic carditis in a microscopy stem.

vis.caption: H and E stained myocardium containing granulomatous Aschoff body with giant cells. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Mitral stenosis** from rheumatic fusion raises left atrial pressure and congests the pulmonary circulation. Atrial fibrillation develops in the enlarged atrium and thrombus may form and embolise. Haemoptysis and hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal compression complete the classic syndrome for exams. **Balloon valvuloplasty** suits a pliable non calcified valve without regurgitation or thrombus, because the balloon splits fused commissures open.
steps.say: Fused mitral leaflets trap pressure inside the left atrium. The lungs become congested and atrial fibrillation develops. Thrombus forms inside the enlarged atrium and may embolise. A pliable valve suits balloon opening of the commissures.

steps.tx: **Infective endocarditis** seeds damaged or prosthetic valves during bacteraemia and builds friable vegetations on the surface. The vegetations contain fibrin, platelets and organisms, and they destroy tissue and embolise widely. **Staphylococcus aureus** attacks even normal valves acutely, while viridans streptococci smoulder subacutely on damaged valves. Duke criteria combine blood cultures, echocardiography and clinical phenomena to structure the diagnosis.
steps.say: Bacteria seed the valves and build friable vegetations there. Staphylococcus aureus is attacking even normal valves with acute illness. Viridans streptococci cause subacute disease on damaged valves. The Duke framework requires blood cultures and echocardiography for diagnosis.

vis.alt: Gross pathology of infective endocarditis showing large, friable vegetations on a heart valve leaflet, with signs of tissue destruction and potential emboli. Illustrates bacterial colonization.
vis.caption: Infective endocarditis: friable vegetations of fibrin, platelets, organisms destroying valve tissue. Image: Mikael Häggström , M.D. Author info - Reusing images - Conflicts of in, CC0/PD, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Calcific **aortic stenosis** of ageing wears and calcifies trileaflet valves or congenital **bicuspid valves** over decades. Outflow obstruction progresses until angina, syncope and heart failure herald high risk. Myxomatous mitral prolapse instead balloons redundant leaflets into the atrium during systole. Prolapse is mostly benign, but severe forms predispose to regurgitation and endocarditis, and systemic diseases can also damage valves.
steps.say: Ageing calcifies the aortic valve and obstructs outflow gradually. Angina, syncope and failure are heralding a high risk stage. Bicuspid valves are calcifying earlier than normal trileaflet valves. Mitral prolapse is ballooning redundant leaflets backward into the atrium.
